text:
Maya: noticed a weird cost/latency spike on route /v2/generate this morning, dashboard shows a lot of traffic attributed to v2 but payloads look like v1 clients (no version header).
Maya: screenshot: https://dash.internal/redwood/route/seq-len?span=1h
Sam: ugh, so implicit routing is choosing the v2 variant because we started prefer-v2-by-capacity yesterday?
Sam: that could make short-seqlen v1 calls suddenly hit bigger models and blow up token costs.
Kevin: can you paste an example request? suspect clients not sending `x-redwood-api-version`.
Maya: example we logged: `{ "prompt": "Summarize...", "max_tokens": null }` —sequence len estimates go high so router thinks it's long-running
Priya: ohhh the router heuristic uses `estimated_seq_len = max_tokens || heuristic_from_prompt(prompt)` and we recently tuned the heuristic to bias toward larger seq for safety
Sam: that change + prefer-v2-by-capacity = explosion.
Maya: deploy-bot: rolling flag revert?
deploy-bot: canary rollback scheduled: feature-flag `route-seqlen-bias` -> off in 5m
Kevin: mitigation plan: 1) flip `route-seqlen-bias` -> off (quick) 2) add explicit telemetry to capture `client-declared-version` vs effective-route 3) console UX: expose per-tenant "tokens-by-declared-version" chart
Priya: for (2) I can add an event `version_mismatch` with fields `tenant_id`, `declared_version`, `routed_variant`, `est_seq_len_bucket` (low/med/high) — minimal payload.
Maya: +1 — that will help quantify how many silent v1 clients are affected.
Sam: for (3) console short-term: add a per-route split on the route dashboard showing "routed by heuristic" vs "routed by header" and token breakdown; I can mock a wireframe.
Priya: I think we also need a temporary quota-protection for unknown-version clients: cap per-tenant tokens routed to higher-cost variants to avoid billing surprises.
Kevin: agree. propose default cap 50k tokens/hr for unknown-version until they opt-in. ops can bump for known enterprise accounts.
Maya: Owners: flip flag — Sam; telemetry event + ingest pipeline — Kevin; console chart mock + small annotation — Priya; quota cap rule — Maya to coordinate with billing.
Sam: I'll flip the flag now and watch metrics.
Sam: done — `route-seqlen-bias=false` on canary, monitoring page: https://infra.internal/flags/route-seqlen-bias
Maya: immediate delta: token-rate down ~48% on canary. nice. :tada:
Kevin: I'll add the `version_mismatch` event to the router and create a minimal Kinesis stream. expect data in ~10m.
Priya: mock for console chart will be in Figma by EOD, adding note to ticket #INF-4923.
Maya: follow-ups: (A) urgent comms to SEs about potential cost exposure for customers who don't set version header (Priya), (B) add short-term billing protection for unknown-version (Maya+Billing), (C) telemetry + long-term routing policy proposal (Kevin).
Maya: pinging @Kevin @Sam @Priya — thanks all, keeping this thread for postmortem notes.
Sam: can we add a tiny server-side header in responses when we route by heuristic so clients see it and can report? `X-Redwood-Routed-By: heuristic`
Kevin: yea easy, I'll attach that to canary responses. helps debugging.
Priya: also add console notice: "We routed this request by heuristic because version header was missing" — small UX nudge.
Maya: +1. recording action items in INF-4923. closing loop after telemetry arrives.
Sam: any objection to making the default router fallback to the lower-cost variant when unknown-version? that's safer but could increase latency for some tenants.
Kevin: tradeoff noted. prefer temporary cap + notification, then discuss long-term default at RFC.
Maya: agreed. prioritizing safety for now.
Priya: thanks — will draft SE message and billing language.
Maya: thanks team. keeping thread pinned until postmortem.
